endorsements.indication_text: First-line systemic therapy for uterine sarcoma; the doxorubicin + trabectedin entry is annotated for leiomyosarcoma (Guide 7 of the patient-guide derivative).
endorsements.version_or_date: v2.2026 (November 2025; verified via the public NCCN patient-guide derivative, subscriber text not reachable this session)

eligibility_rationale: Systemic-therapy naive with this exact regimen already planned, so nothing in the record argues against it; the conditions are the profile's own named open items: baseline echocardiogram before doxorubicin, hepatic and renal panels before trabectedin, an altitude-referenced pulmonary and oximetry baseline (she lives at about 8,500 ft), and confirmation of the assumed ECOG 1.
blocking_factors: No baseline LVEF/echocardiogram on file; the profile names it mandatory before doxorubicin
No hepatic or renal labs on file; trabectedin carries hepatotoxicity
Pulmonary reserve and oximetry not yet assessed against high-altitude residence
ECOG 1 is an unverified intake assumption

evidence.design: randomised open-label phase 3 vs doxorubicin alone
evidence.population: first-line advanced or metastatic leiomyosarcoma (uterine 45% stratification stratum)

evidence.design: final OS analysis of the same phase 3

toxicity_highlights: Grade 3-4 neutropenia 80%, thrombocytopenia 47%, febrile neutropenia 28% (vs 13%, 0% and 9% with doxorubicin alone); one treatment-related death in the trial
Anthracycline cardiotoxicity; cumulative dose planning matters from cycle 1
Trabectedin hepatotoxicity and rare rhabdomyolysis; central line required

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: Contains no gemcitabine, so it preserves the seat on the abemaciclib + gem/doc trial (NCT06498648, Experimental rank 3), which off-protocol gemcitabine would permanently close. Each cycle also draws down two anthracycline ceilings: peposertib (NCT05711615) requires cumulative doxorubicin of 360 mg/m2 or less, exactly six LMS-04 cycles at 60 mg/m2, and in-vivo lung perfusion (NCT02811523) excludes more than 450 mg cumulative. The induction cycle count is a before-cycle-1 decision; a five-cycle plan is a choice made up front, not at cycle six.

rationale: The regimen the consulting sarcoma oncologist has already planned, and the board's first choice on four of five slates: in LMS-04, adding trabectedin to doxorubicin with a trabectedin maintenance phase roughly doubled median PFS (HR 0.41, 95% CI 0.29-0.58) and extended median OS to 33 vs 24 months (adjusted HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.44-0.95) in first-line advanced leiomyosarcoma, and NCCN now carries it as a preferred first-line option for uterine LMS. Two caveats carry weight: uterine primaries were a 45% stratification stratum and no uterine-only effect size has been published, so the headline numbers are trial-wide rather than uterine-specific; and the toxicity price (80% grade 3-4 neutropenia, 28% febrile neutropenia) has not been put to her, since every preference on file is an intake default she never stated. The named baseline workup (echo, hepatic panel, altitude-referenced oximetry, a documented ECOG) belongs before cycle 1.
notes: The combination is not FDA-approved as a regimen; both components are approved drugs (doxorubicin on-label for metastatic soft tissue sarcoma, trabectedin for L-sarcomas after an anthracycline) and the first-line carriage is guideline-based.

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: Off-protocol gemcitabine permanently closes NCT06498648 (abemaciclib + gem/doc, Experimental rank 3), which admits treatment-naive patients; the trial is the protocolised way to receive this same backbone. LMS-04 contains no gemcitabine and leaves that seat open, an asymmetry that belongs in the first-line conversation. Choosing gem/doc off protocol spends none of the anthracycline ceilings the doxorubicin-based options draw down.

rationale: The other NCCN-preferred first-line option for uterine LMS and the historical US default, with real single-arm first-line activity in this exact histology (ORR 35.8%, 90% CI 23.5-49.6). The randomised footing is sobering: in GeDDiS it was not superior to doxorubicin and the PFS hazard ratio of 1.28 (95% CI 0.99-1.65) trended worse, which is part of why the board's slates centred on the doxorubicin-trabectedin backbone instead. Its main sequencing property is what it closes: any off-protocol gemcitabine permanently forecloses the abemaciclib + gem/doc trial seat.
notes: GOG-0250 tested bevacizumab added to this backbone in chemotherapy-naive uLMS and was negative (PFS HR 1.12, p=0.58); the bevacizumab variant is assessed and set aside as its own row.

Contains no gemcitabine, so the abemaciclib + gem/doc trial seat stays open.

rationale: The intensified first-line doublet for a patient in whom response, not just control, is the goal: EORTC 62012 doubled the response rate (26% vs 14%) and improved PFS, but overall survival did not move (HR 0.83, 95.5% CI 0.67-1.03) and febrile neutropenia reached 46% despite pegfilgrastim. NCCN carries it as a preferred first-line option for uterine sarcoma, so it stays a live alternative where cytoreduction toward local therapy is the aim. The response-for-toxicity trade is exactly the kind of decision the record shows has not yet been discussed with her.

rationale: Single-agent doxorubicin is the on-label, guideline-preferred backbone that both LMS-04 and EORTC 62012 improved on in PFS or response without ever beating it decisively on survival until LMS-04's final analysis, and it remains the gentlest of the preferred first-line options (febrile neutropenia around 9-13% vs 28% and 46% for the combinations). For a patient whose efficacy-toxicity weighting is an unstated intake default, it is the fallback the combinations have to justify themselves against. NCCN's uterine sarcoma list carries it as preferred, and its label covers metastatic soft tissue sarcoma outright.
notes: NCCN's preferred first-line list also carries doxorubicin + dacarbazine, annotated for LMS and for patients who cannot receive ifosfamide; it is not broken out as a separate row here because the decision it serves (an anthracycline doublet without ifosfamide) is covered by this row and the two combination rows.

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: The in-vivo lung perfusion trial (NCT02811523, Experimental rank 5) and pulmonary suffusion are metastasectomy-plus-perfusion packages occupying this same post-induction local-therapy slot; IVLP excludes cumulative doxorubicin above 450 mg, so the induction plan chosen now decides whether the surgical route can still be the trial version or only the standard one.

rationale: Resection of limited lung metastases is the one standard route to long-term survival this disease offers (5-year OS 55.4% in the uterine-primary registry; median OS 70 months in selected LMS series), which is why the treating oncologist kept it on the table after systemic control. The honesty constraint is that those figures belong to complete resections of countable nodules, and her current imaging shows the opposite phenotype: bilateral, infiltrative, possibly inflammatory. Whether induction converts her into the population the series describe is a question for restaging, and the stakes of that reassessment are high because this is the closest thing to a curative-intent move on either table.

rationale: The non-surgical route to local control of limited lung disease, carried by NCCN's uterine sarcoma pathway for patients with few metastatic tumours, with high local-control figures in sarcoma-specific series (24-month local failure 7.4%, 95% CI 4.0-13.9). Both supporting series are retrospective and selected, so the reported absence of severe toxicity is an artefact-prone estimate rather than a guarantee, and her infiltrative bilateral disease is not yet an SBRT geometry. Like metastasectomy, this becomes a real decision at restaging after induction.

Carried so the report shows both label routes through the same door; closing the MMR gate is one tissue IHC on material that already exists.

endorsements.designation: on-label approval (tumor-agnostic)
endorsements.indication_text: Adult and pediatric patients with solid tumors that have an NTRK gene fusion without a known acquired resistance mutation, are metastatic or where surgical resection is likely to result in severe morbidity, and have no satisfactory alternative treatments or that have progressed following treatment.
endorsements.version_or_date: current label via openFDA, retrieved August 2026

endorsements.designation: First-line, therapies used in certain circumstances: 'TKI therapy for NTRK gene fusion-positive tumors: Larotrectinib (Vitrakvi)'
endorsements.indication_text: First-line systemic therapy for uterine sarcoma, restricted to NTRK fusion-positive tumours (Guide 7 of the patient-guide derivative; entrectinib and repotrectinib are listed alongside).
endorsements.version_or_date: v2.2026 (November 2025; verified via the public NCCN patient-guide derivative, subscriber text not reachable this session)

eligibility_rationale: Everything turns on a fusion that has never been tested at decision-relevant resolution: the plasma panel's non-detection at an unsupplied tumor fraction is not exclusionary, and no RNA-based or tissue fusion assay has been run.
blocking_factors: NTRK fusion status unmeasured on tissue; plasma non-detection at unknown tumor fraction does not exclude a fusion

biomarker_requirement.threshold: NTRK gene fusion without a known acquired resistance mutation, by an FDA-approved or equivalent assay (RNA-based fusion panel preferred)

evidence.design: pooled analysis of three phase 1/2 trials
evidence.effect_size: ORR 79% (95% CI 72-85), 16% complete responses; grade 3-4 treatment-related events each at 3% or below

toxicity_highlights: Generally mild: transaminase rises, dizziness, fatigue; withdrawal pain on stopping
rationale: A tumor-agnostic approval with dramatic response rates (ORR 79%, 95% CI 72-85) that NCCN carries even at first line for fusion-positive uterine sarcoma, sitting behind a biomarker that is vanishingly rare in leiomyosarcoma and has never been properly tested here. The plasma panel's silence does not close the question, because fusion detection in plasma is insensitive at low tumor fraction; an RNA-based fusion assay on the existing tissue would settle it. Low priority reflects the prior probability, not the drug.

endorsements.designation: Bevacizumab carried for a different sarcoma histology: 'Solitary fibrous tumor: Bevacizumab and temozolomide' (Soft Tissue Sarcoma guideline)
endorsements.indication_text: Bevacizumab-containing therapy appears in the soft tissue sarcoma guideline for solitary fibrous tumor; the current uterine-sarcoma systemic lists (first- and second-line, v2.2026 derivative) do not carry bevacizumab in any combination.
endorsements.version_or_date: v1.2025 (May 2025; verified via the public NCCN patient-guide derivative, subscriber text not reachable this session)

eligibility_rationale: No medical bar in the record; the reason this row is set aside is evidential and regulatory, not eligibility.

evidence.design: randomised double-blind placebo-controlled phase 3, first line
evidence.effect_size: Bevacizumab added nothing: PFS HR 1.12 (p=0.58; mPFS 6.2 mo placebo vs 4.2 mo bevacizumab), OS HR 1.07 (p=0.81); accrual stopped early for futility

toxicity_highlights: Bevacizumab added grade 3 hypertension (8% vs 0%) and a fistula in GOG-0250, with no efficacy return
rationale: Assessed because the routing worklist carried it, and set aside on its own randomised evidence: GOG-0250 tested exactly this regimen in exactly this population, chemotherapy-naive metastatic uterine LMS, and stopped early for futility with the hazard ratios pointing the wrong way. Bevacizumab holds no FDA sarcoma indication, and the current uterine-sarcoma guideline lists do not carry it, so the plain gem/doc row above is the live version of this backbone.

endorsements.designation: Anti-estrogen therapy for hormone receptor-positive uterine sarcoma; Guide 8 lists aromatase inhibitors as preferred for low-grade ESS and low-risk adenosarcoma
endorsements.indication_text: Uterine sarcoma that is hormone receptor-positive: anti-estrogen therapy may be recommended; the preferred anti-estrogen list (aromatase inhibitors, with or without GnRH analog) is written for low-grade ESS and low-risk adenosarcoma.
endorsements.version_or_date: v2.2026 (November 2025; verified via the public NCCN patient-guide derivative, subscriber text not reachable this session)

eligibility_rationale: Her tumor is ER and PR <1% by IHC, a confirmed decision-relevant negative; the activity of aromatase inhibition in uLMS is specific to ER-positive disease, so the receptor result closes this door rather than leaving it ajar.
blocking_factors: ER <1% and PR <1% by IHC, confirmed; the endorsement requires hormone receptor-positive disease
rationale: Included so the absence of endocrine therapy reads as a decision, not an oversight: anti-estrogen therapy is the guideline's carve-out for hormone receptor-positive uterine sarcoma, and her confirmed ER/PR <1% takes her out of that population. This is the one standard-of-care door her existing biomarker results have already closed.
